recipes.title: Huevos a la flamenca, light
recipes.summary: Spanish baked eggs with cured pork, peppers and spinach in a rich tomato sauce. Extra vegetables and less pork and oil keep this keto breakfast generous but lighter.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C so the eggs begin cooking as soon as the dish goes in.
Prepare the onion, bell pepper, garlic and spinach in their listed sizes.
Heat the olive oil in a wide ovenproof pan over medium heat.
Cook the onion, bell pepper and cured pork until the vegetables soften and the pork edges colour.
Add the garlic and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and salt and simmer until the sauce is thick enough to hold shallow wells.
Fold the spinach into the tomato sauce until wilted.
Crack the eggs into the wells and bake until the whites are set and the yolks remain tender.
Rest the huevos a la flamenca briefly before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served immediately while the yolks are tender. Refrigerate the tomato and pork base for up to 3 days, then reheat it and cook fresh eggs in the sauce.

recipes.title: Huevos a la flamenca
recipes.summary: Spanish eggs baked in a savoury tomato sauce with cured pork, peppers, onion and paprika. The softly set yolks make this a satisfying keto breakfast for sharing.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C so the eggs begin cooking as soon as the dish goes in.
Prepare the onion, bell pepper, garlic and spinach in their listed sizes.
Heat the olive oil in a wide ovenproof pan over medium heat.
Cook the onion, bell pepper and cured pork until the vegetables soften and the pork is lightly browned.
Add the garlic and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and salt and simmer until the sauce is rich and spoonable.
Fold the spinach into the tomato sauce until wilted.
Crack the eggs into shallow wells and bake until the whites are set and the yolks remain tender.
Rest the huevos a la flamenca briefly before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Serve straight from the oven for the best egg texture. Refrigerate the cooked sauce base for up to 3 days and add freshly cracked eggs when reheating.

recipes.title: Huevos a la flamenca, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Spanish breakfast of baked eggs, cured pork, peppers and spinach in a deeply savoury tomato sauce. Extra eggs and pork make it substantial while remaining keto.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C so the larger egg dish begins cooking immediately.
Prepare the onion, bell pepper, garlic and spinach in their listed sizes.
Heat the olive oil in a large ovenproof pan over medium heat.
Cook the onion, bell pepper and cured pork until the vegetables soften and the pork is deeply golden at the edges.
Add the garlic and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and salt and simmer until the sauce is thick and rich.
Fold the spinach into the tomato sauce until evenly wilted.
Crack the eggs into shallow wells and bake until the whites are set and the yolks reach your preferred consistency.
Rest the huevos a la flamenca briefly before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten freshly baked. Refrigerate the tomato and pork mixture for up to 3 days, then reheat and add fresh eggs before serving.

recipes.title: Chicken fatteh, light
recipes.summary: Crisp pita, warm chickpeas and roasted chicken layered with lemony tahini yogurt. Extra cucumber and less bread and sauce keep this Middle Eastern lunch fresh and Mediterranean.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Cut the pita bread into bite-size pieces and spread it across a baking tray.
Bake the pita bread until crisp and lightly golden.
Coat the chicken breast with the olive oil, cumin, paprika and half the salt.
Roast the chicken breast until the breast is cooked through and lightly browned.
Warm the chickpeas, canned, in a small pan until hot, then drain them.
Whisk the greek yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and remaining salt until smooth.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until lightly golden.
Slice the cucumber and rest the chicken breast before cutting it into pieces.
Layer the pita bread, chickpeas, chicken breast and yogurt sauce in a serving dish.
Finish the chicken fatteh with the cucumber and pine nuts.

recipes.storageNotes: Best assembled just before serving so the pita remains crisp. Refrigerate the chicken, chickpeas and yogurt sauce separately for up to 3 days. Do not freeze the assembled dish.

recipes.title: Chicken fatteh
recipes.summary: A layered Middle Eastern lunch of crisp pita, chickpeas, roasted chicken and creamy lemon-tahini yogurt. Toasted pine nuts add the traditional warm, nutty finish.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Cut the pita bread into bite-size pieces and spread it across a baking tray.
Bake the pita bread until crisp and golden.
Coat the chicken thigh with the olive oil, cumin, paprika and half the salt.
Roast the chicken thigh until the thigh is tender, browned and cooked through.
Warm the chickpeas, canned, in a small pan until hot, then drain them.
Whisk the greek yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and remaining salt until smooth.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden and fragrant.
Slice the cucumber and rest the chicken thigh before cutting it into pieces.
Layer the pita bread, chickpeas, chicken thigh and yogurt sauce in a serving dish.
Finish the chicken fatteh with the cucumber and pine nuts.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep the pita separate from the chicken, chickpeas and yogurt sauce for up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken and chickpeas, then assemble. The finished fatteh is not suitable for freezing.

recipes.title: Chicken fatteh, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous platter of crisp pita, tender chicken, chickpeas and creamy tahini yogurt. Extra chicken, bread and pine nuts make this a substantial Mediterranean-style lunch.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Cut the pita bread into bite-size pieces and spread it across two baking trays.
Bake the pita bread until crisp and deeply golden.
Coat the chicken thigh with the olive oil, cumin, paprika and half the salt.
Roast the chicken thigh until the thigh is tender, browned and cooked through.
Warm the chickpeas, canned, in a saucepan until hot, then drain them.
Whisk the greek yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and remaining salt until smooth and creamy.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden and fragrant.
Slice the cucumber and rest the chicken thigh before cutting it into pieces.
Layer the pita bread, chickpeas, chicken thigh and yogurt sauce in a large serving dish.
Finish the chicken fatteh with the cucumber and pine nuts.

recipes.storageNotes: Store all components separately for up to 3 days and assemble after reheating the chicken and chickpeas. The pita and cucumber are best fresh. Do not freeze the assembled dish.

recipes.title: Black bean enchiladas, light
recipes.summary: Vegan enchiladas filled with black beans, peppers and zucchini under a smoky tomato sauce. Fewer tortillas and extra vegetables keep the dinner lighter without shrinking the plate.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Prepare the onion, bell pepper, zucchini, garlic and cilantro in their listed sizes.
Heat half the olive oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, cumin and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, vegetable broth and half the salt and simmer until the enchilada sauce thickens.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a wide pan and cook the bell pepper and zucchini until softened and lightly browned.
Fold the black beans and remaining salt through the vegetables until hot.
Fill the tortilla with the black bean mixture and roll each one tightly.
Arrange the tortilla rolls in a baking dish and cover them with the tomato sauce.
Bake the enchiladas until bubbling and lightly crisp at the edges.
Finish the black bean enchiladas with the cilantro.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat covered until hot throughout. Freeze baked enchiladas for up to 2 months, although the tortillas will soften slightly.

recipes.title: Black bean enchiladas
recipes.summary: Soft tortillas packed with black beans and vegetables, baked beneath a cumin and paprika tomato sauce. These Mexican-style enchiladas are hearty, savoury and completely vegan.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Add the tomatoes, canned, vegetable broth and half the salt and simmer until the enchilada sauce becomes rich.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a wide pan and cook the bell pepper and zucchini until lightly browned.

recipes.title: Black bean enchiladas, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous tray of vegan enchiladas loaded with extra black beans and tortillas under a rich smoky tomato sauce. It makes a substantial Mexican dinner for four.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Prepare the onion, bell pepper, zucchini, garlic and cilantro in their listed sizes.
Heat half the olive oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, cumin and paprika and stir until darkened and fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, vegetable broth and half the salt and simmer until the enchilada sauce is rich and thick.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a large pan and cook the bell pepper and zucchini until browned at the edges.
Fold the black beans and remaining salt through the vegetables until thoroughly hot.
Fill the tortilla generously with the black bean mixture and roll each one tightly.
Arrange the tortilla rolls across two baking dishes and cover them with the tomato sauce.
Bake the enchiladas until bubbling and deeply coloured at the edges.
Finish the black bean enchiladas with the cilantro.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days and reheat covered until bubbling. Freeze baked enchiladas for up to 2 months in well-sealed portions.

recipes.title: Brazilian rice fritters, light
recipes.summary: Golden Brazilian-style rice fritters with eggs, parmesan, spinach and spring onions. Less rice, cheese and oil plus extra spinach keep the snack lighter and still satisfying.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then spread it on a tray to cool and dry slightly.
Prepare the spinach, spring onions and garlic while the rice cools.
Wilt the spinach in a dry pan until its moisture evaporates.
Mix the white rice, eggs, parmesan cheese, wheat flour, spinach, spring onions, garlic, paprika and salt into a thick mixture.
Shape the rice mixture into twelve compact fritters.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium heat.
Fry the rice fritters until golden and crisp on both sides, working in batches.
Drain the Brazilian rice fritters briefly on absorbent paper.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served freshly fried. Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot oven or dry pan. Freeze cooked fritters for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Brazilian rice fritters, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous batch of Brazilian rice fritters with extra rice, eggs and parmesan. The deeply golden fritters make a substantial vegetarian snack for sharing.

Shape the rice mixture into twenty compact fritters.

recipes.title: Ethiopian chechebsa, light
recipes.summary: Torn Ethiopian flatbread tossed with fragrant paprika, cumin, ginger and garlic butter, served with cool Greek yogurt. Less butter and flour keep this breakfast lighter.

steps.instruction: Mix the wheat flour, water and half the salt into a soft dough.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic.
Rest the dough covered so the wheat flour hydrates and becomes easier to roll.
Divide and roll the dough into two thin flatbreads.
Cook each flatbread in a dry pan until browned in spots and cooked through.
Tear the flatbreads into bite-size pieces while still warm.
Melt the butter with the paprika, cumin, ginger, garlic and remaining salt until fragrant.
Toss the torn flatbread through the spiced butter until evenly coated.
Serve the Ethiopian chechebsa with the greek yogurt.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served immediately while the flatbread is warm. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a pan with a splash of water. Keep the Greek yogurt separate.

recipes.summary: Warm torn flatbread coated in spiced butter with paprika, cumin, ginger and garlic, then served with cool Greek yogurt. It is a comforting Ethiopian breakfast for two.

Knead the dough until smooth and elastic.
Rest the dough covered so the wheat flour hydrates and becomes easier to roll.
Divide and roll the dough into three thin flatbreads.
Cook each flatbread in a dry pan until browned in spots and cooked through.
Tear the flatbreads into bite-size pieces while still warm.

recipes.title: Ethiopian chechebsa, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Ethiopian breakfast of torn flatbread richly coated with spiced butter and served with plenty of cool Greek yogurt. The larger portion is warm and deeply satisfying.

steps.instruction: Mix the wheat flour, water and half the salt into a soft dough.
Knead the larger dough until smooth and elastic.
Rest the dough covered so the wheat flour hydrates fully.
Divide and roll the dough into four thin flatbreads.
Cook each flatbread in a dry pan until browned in spots and cooked through.
Tear the flatbreads into generous bite-size pieces while warm.
Melt the butter with the paprika, cumin, ginger, garlic and remaining salt until fragrant.
Toss the torn flatbread through the spiced butter until every piece is coated.
Serve the Ethiopian chechebsa with the greek yogurt.

recipes.storageNotes: Best eaten hot from the pan. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat with a little water or butter. Keep the Greek yogurt chilled and separate.
